lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Auto Parts | Mechanical Design Engineer | Metro City, Country | Jun 2025 - Present
- Designed stamping dies for automotive brackets in SolidWorks, cutting the scrap rate from 6% to 4% on two press lines.
- Ran tolerance stack-up analyses for 12 production parts and signed off first-article inspections with the supplier.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: There is no quick explanation of the target role or how the ML work, mechanical-design job, and degree connect.
items.because: A reader may not know whether the résumé is aimed at ML engineering, mechanical design, or both.

items.says: Clarify how the in-progress master’s degree fits with a current job in another country.
items.because: A reviewer may wonder how the locations and dates fit together.

items.says: Consider the current mechanical-design role’s placement for an ML application.
items.because: It may be less relevant than the ML work, though the chronology should not be misleading.

items.says: Expand the skills section selectively for the intended role.
items.because: It is short relative to the technical experience and projects.

items.says: Use the project responsibility labels consistently and precisely.
items.because: They should help the reader assess ownership accurately.

items.says: The email and web address look like placeholders.
items.because: Literal placeholders should be replaced with professional contact details and a direct portfolio or code-profile link.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It does not establish qualifications and can introduce unnecessary bias.

items.says: Remove nationality in most cases.
items.because: It does not establish qualifications and can introduce unnecessary bias.

items.says: Make the school location unambiguous in the submitted version.
items.because: The generic city and country labels may not be clear unless they are only anonymized for this review.

items.says: Make the school location unambiguous in the submitted version.
items.because: The generic city and country labels may not be clear unless they are only anonymized for this review.

items.says: Explain the current mechanical-design role’s connection to the target role.
items.because: It appears alongside substantial ML experience and projects, leaving the reader to guess why it is there.

items.says: Give the scrap-rate improvement more scope, such as production volume or time period, if substantiated.
items.because: Readers may want that context to judge the result.

items.says: Add the inspection work’s result or consequence if it can be supported.
items.because: The bullet names the work but does not show its outcome.

items.says: Define the diagnostic-accuracy metric, evaluation set, and comparison point.
items.because: A technical reviewer may question what the 35% improvement measures and whether it is relative or absolute.

items.says: Define what counted as reviewer disagreement and how it was measured.
items.because: The reduction is useful evidence only if its meaning is clear.

items.says: Define the evaluation behind the baseline, equal-accuracy, and latency comparison.
items.because: The GRPO result should be easy to interpret.

items.says: Make the specialized terminology legible to a general recruiter.
items.because: It may not be immediately understandable outside a technical audience.

items.says: Explain what the two regressions would have affected and how the harness informed release decisions.
items.because: The bullet shows useful work but leaves its impact unclear.

items.says: Remove or consolidate the repeated assistant-only-loss-masking point.
items.because: The earlier bullet already ties that method to an outcome, while this one adds no separate result.

items.says: The triage backlog achievement is duplicated in the evaluation-framework project.
items.because: Crediting the same result twice can look like double-counting.

items.says: Clarify ownership of the triage result.
items.because: The same work is also credited to a project labeled Contributor.

items.says: Give the backlog’s starting scale if reliable figures are available.
items.because: The time window after launch does not establish the backlog’s initial scope.

items.says: Specify the model, workload, or training setup behind the 4× GPU-memory reduction.
items.because: The result’s value depends on those conditions.

items.says: Clarify whether the precision change affected quality or training behavior.
items.because: That helps explain the conditions behind the memory result.

items.says: The CI bullet switches to present tense in a past role.
items.because: Its tense is inconsistent with the role dates.

items.says: Define the release cycle and give a before-and-after comparison if available.
items.because: “Shortened release cycles to 3 days” does not establish the metric’s basis.

items.says: Add a measurable consequence of the fleet-services migration if available.
items.because: The bullet gives no frequency, scale, or operational impact for the dispatch delays.

items.says: Remove or substantiate the broad AI-first-practices claim.
items.because: It has no measure, concrete deliverable, or defined adoption evidence and dilutes the technical bullets.

items.says: Clarify what grew 100×, what was measured, and whether task success was maintained.
items.because: The context-window stress-test result is ambiguous.

items.says: State the concurrency test conditions or how the fix was verified if space permits.
items.because: That would make the deadlock and lost-result claim easier to assess.

items.says: Explain which two quantities the Kendall correlation relates.
items.because: Reviewers need to know why 0.89 indicates the evaluator worked well.

items.says: The triage backlog achievement duplicates the internship result.
items.because: The same result is credited in two places and can look like double-counting.

items.says: Clarify the project’s contribution to the triage system.
items.because: This entry says Contributor while the internship says the system was built there.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific.
items.because: A target-role reader will look for the concrete methods and tools used.
